data.title: Ship Ergo View v0.1
Build the Ergo data and command adapter
data.body:
## Goal
- Load an Ergo repository into a stable, UI-oriented snapshot without importing Ergo internals.
- Route every write through the official `ergo` executable so Ergo continues to own locking and mutation invariants.

## Context
- Ergo View is a separate Go module and cannot import `github.com/sandover/ergo/internal/ergo`.
- Support `.ergo/plans.jsonl` and the legacy `.ergo/events.jsonl` filename used by Ergo itself.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Repository discovery accepts the current directory, `--dir`, a repository path, or an `.ergo` directory.
- JSONL replay reconstructs tasks, containers, dependencies, reverse dependencies, readiness, claims, messages, results, and tombstones needed by the UI.
- A truncated final JSONL record is tolerated; malformed complete records produce a path-and-line error.
- Snapshot values are immutable to callers and ordered deterministically.
- A command runner executes explicit argument vectors without a shell, captures readable errors, and supports cancellation.
- Contract fixtures cover current Ergo 3 events plus legacy container and error-state records.

## Validation Gates
- `go test -race ./internal/ergo`
- `go test -race ./...`

data.title: Build the responsive outline and detail experience
data.body:
## Goal
- Deliver the polished default Ergo View experience for quickly browsing work and reading full task context.

## Acceptance Criteria
- `ev [--dir path] [--agent identity]` opens an alternate-screen Bubble Tea 2 application.
- Wide terminals show a work outline and Markdown detail pane; narrow terminals provide focused full-screen panes without clipped content.
- The outline presents containers, progress, state, readiness, task IDs, and claim identities with accessible color plus text/symbol cues.
- The detail pane renders body Markdown, dependencies, dependents, lifecycle messages, and result paths.
- Vim keys, arrow keys, page navigation, mouse selection/scrolling, contextual help, and clean quit behavior work consistently.
- The theme adapts to light and dark terminals and respects `NO_COLOR`.

## Validation Gates
- `go test -race ./internal/ui`
- `go build ./cmd/ev`
- `go test -race ./...`

data.title: Add board, dependency, search, and live-reload workflows
data.body:
## Goal
- Let humans move fluidly between project flow, task hierarchy, and dependency context.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Overview, board, and dependency views share the same selected task and current filters.
- The board groups leaves into ready, waiting, doing, blocked, done, and canceled states without conflating dependency waiting with explicit blocking.
- The dependency view clearly separates prerequisites, the selected task, and work it unlocks.
- Fuzzy search matches IDs, titles, bodies, and claim identities with immediate feedback.
- State/container filters compose predictably and can be cleared in one action.
- The active JSONL file is watched or polled portably; external Ergo changes reload without losing a still-valid selection.
- Empty repositories, empty filters, removed selections, and concurrent partial appends produce useful UI states rather than panics.

## Validation Gates
- `go test -race ./internal/ui`
- `go test -race ./...`

data.title: Add task creation, editing, graph, and lifecycle actions
data.body:
## Goal
- Cover everyday Ergo interaction from the TUI while preserving Ergo as the sole writer.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Dialogs support creating leaves and container plans, renaming, replacing Markdown bodies, moving leaves, and adding or removing dependency edges.
- Claim prompts for an identity when `--agent` is absent and remembers it for the running session.
- Done, block, cancel, and release support lifecycle messages and optional result paths where Ergo permits them.
- Actions validate required input locally, show the exact selected target, and require confirmation for canceling or resuming closed work.
- The adapter invokes only official Ergo 3 commands with explicit arguments and stdin; it never edits JSONL directly.
- Success reloads the snapshot and preserves focus; command failures remain visible and do not dismiss the user’s input.
- Dialog reducer tests cover validation, confirmation, cancellation, success, and subprocess failure.

## Validation Gates
- `go test -race ./internal/ergo ./internal/ui`
- `go test -race ./...`

data.title: Polish, package, and document Ergo View
data.body:
## Goal
- Make the new public repository installable, visually demonstrable, and safe across Ergo’s supported platforms.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Render snapshots cover narrow, standard, and wide layouts; Unicode titles, long Markdown, light/dark themes, and `NO_COLOR`.
- README documents requirements, `go install github.com/jamestjsp/ergoview/cmd/ev@latest`, release archives, discovery, all views, actions, and key bindings.
- Committed screenshots show the overview, board, and dependency experiences using realistic sample data.
- CI runs formatting, vetting, and race-enabled tests on Linux, macOS, and Windows, and builds `ev` on all three.
- GoReleaser produces `ev`/`ev.exe` archives for AMD64 and ARM64 where supported.
- `ev --help` is concise, complete, and accurate.
- No generated binaries, temporary fixtures, or TUI logs are committed.

## Validation Gates
- `go mod tidy`
- `go vet ./...`
- `go test -race ./...`
- `go build ./cmd/ev`
- `goreleaser check`

## Scope
- Build a polished, responsive Bubble Tea companion for viewing and managing Ergo repositories.
- Ship it from the separate public `jamestjsp/ergoview` repository.
- Present outline, board, and focused dependency views plus everyday task mutations.

## Decisions
- Product name: Ergo View.
- Executable: `ev` on macOS and Linux, `ev.exe` on Windows.
- Use stable Bubble Tea 2, Bubbles 2, Lip Gloss 2, and Glamour 2 packages.
- Read Ergo's documented append-only JSONL format for UI snapshots.
- Route every mutation through the official Ergo 3 executable; never write event records directly.
- Support current and legacy Ergo event-log filenames.
- Ship from this repository through `go install` and cross-platform release archives.

## Constraints
- Preserve the distinction between explicit blocked work and todo work waiting on dependencies.
- Keep UI state responsive while subprocess and reload work runs asynchronously.
- Remain portable across macOS, Linux, and Windows.
- Test behavior and rendered layouts persistently.

## Non-goals
- Prune or compact actions.
- PageRank, critical-path scoring, robot APIs, or other Beads Viewer analytics.
- Reimplementing Ergo's mutation validation or lock protocol.
- A web UI, daemon, or network service.

data.text: Implemented current and legacy JSONL replay, derived UI snapshots, and a cancellable official-command runner. Verified with race-enabled package and repository tests.

Built the responsive Bubble Tea 2 outline/detail shell with adaptive theming, Markdown, keyboard and mouse navigation, and narrow/wide layouts. Verified through race-enabled UI tests and live TTY checks at 80 and 140 columns.

Added overview, six-state board, and focused dependency views with shared selection; fuzzy search; composable state/container filters; and portable live reload. Verified race-enabled tests and live wide-terminal view switching.
Implemented and smoke-tested create, claim, done, block, cancel, release, edit, move, and dependency actions through the official Ergo CLI.
Added deterministic render snapshots and README screenshots, CI and release workflows, complete install/use docs, and verified all six GoReleaser targets.

data.title: Make dependency graphs intuitive
Build the adaptive dependency layout engine
data.body:
## Goal
- Turn an Ergo snapshot into a deterministic, terminal-sized dependency layout independent of rendering.
- Preserve dependency direction while fitting the most useful neighborhood around the selected node.

## Context
- Ergo graphs are acyclic and may include containers as dependency endpoints.
- Graphviz `dot` and ELK Layered both use hierarchical layers for directed graphs, with crossing and edge-length reduction.
- The default scope should remain useful without asking users to configure graph depth.

## Acceptance Criteria
- A focused graph projection includes the selected node, then expands upstream and downstream breadth-first until the available cell budget is exhausted.
- Hidden branches are represented by stable overflow summaries instead of silently disappearing.
- Nodes are assigned deterministic topological ranks; repeated barycentric sweeps reduce avoidable crossings without changing dependency direction.
- The layout chooses left-to-right or top-to-bottom orientation from available width, height, node dimensions, and visible rank count rather than one fixed breakpoint.
- Ordering is stable across renders and snapshot reloads when the graph has not structurally changed.
- Tasks, containers, dependency edges, and parent membership remain separate concepts in the layout model.
- Diamond, fan-in, fan-out, long-chain, disconnected, multi-container, Unicode-title, tiny-terminal, and large-graph fixtures are covered.
- Layout remains responsive on a synthetic 1,000-node DAG.

## Validation Gates
- `go test -race ./internal/ui -run 'TestGraph|TestAdaptiveGraphLayout'`
- `go test ./internal/ui -run '^$' -bench BenchmarkAdaptiveGraphLayout`
- `go test -race ./...`

data.title: Render an epic-aware Unicode graph canvas
data.body:
## Goal
- Replace the current three-list dependency screen with an elegant node-and-edge graph.
- Make tasks, epics, state, readiness, and graph direction understandable without relying on color.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Nodes render as compact cards with title, ID, and state/readiness; selected and focused nodes remain unmistakable in light, dark, and `NO_COLOR` modes.
- Container cards use distinct shape and progress treatment; child task cards show their container identity without drawing containment as a dependency edge.
- Dependency edges use orthogonal Unicode routing, directional arrowheads, and correct junction glyphs without crossing through node text.
- Wide layouts use horizontal flow when it exposes more ranks; tall or narrow layouts use vertical flow when it exposes more useful context.
- Overflow summaries state how many upstream or downstream nodes are hidden and can serve as exploration targets.
- The empty, isolated-node, missing-reference, and too-small-terminal states remain legible and actionable.
- Golden renders cover narrow, standard, wide, light, dark, and no-color layouts with multi-epic branching data.

## Validation Gates
- `go test -race ./internal/ui -run 'TestGraphCanvas|TestRenderSnapshots'`
- `go test -race ./...`

data.title: Add spatial node exploration and graph focus controls
data.body:
## Goal
- Let users understand a dependency chain by moving through it naturally rather than returning to a list.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Arrow keys and `h`/`j`/`k`/`l` move to the nearest graph node in the requested screen direction using deterministic spatial scoring.
- Selecting a node updates the shared Ergo selection, node styling, action target, and status context.
- `enter` focuses the selected node and re-expands the adaptive neighborhood; `esc` returns to the previous focus when available.
- A single depth control cycles direct, adaptive, and full-lineage scopes, and the active scope is visible.
- Mouse clicks select visible node cards; clicks on blank canvas do not change selection.
- Selection stays visible after resize, filtering, external reload, or a completed action when the task still exists.
- Navigation skips edge cells and overflow summaries unless an overflow summary can reveal additional nodes.
- Help and footer hints are contextual to graph mode and remain compact at narrow widths.

## Validation Gates
- `go test -race ./internal/ui -run 'TestGraphNavigation|TestGraphMouse|TestGraphFocus'`
- `go test -race ./...`

data.title: Polish and document the graph-first dependency experience
data.body:
## Goal
- Ship the graph as a coherent public feature with realistic examples, complete documentation, and cross-platform visual confidence.

## Acceptance Criteria
- The render fixture demonstrates a multi-epic graph with a long chain, fan-in, fan-out, a blocked task, parallel ready tasks, and dependencies on completed containers.
- README and in-app help explain dependency direction, task versus epic visuals, adaptive scope, focus history, keyboard navigation, and mouse behavior succinctly.
- The dependency documentation image is regenerated from the tested render fixture and shows the new graph rather than the old three-column list.
- Snapshot and behavioral tests protect cell-width handling, Unicode titles, resize transitions, deterministic layout, selection persistence, and `NO_COLOR`.
- Formatting, vetting, race tests, build, and GoReleaser validation pass.
- Live TTY checks at approximately 70x24, 100x30, and 140x36 confirm that the graph uses the available real estate without clipping or corrupting edges.

## Validation Gates
- `gofmt -w internal/ui`
- `go vet ./...`
- `go test -race ./...`
- `go build ./cmd/ev`
- `goreleaser check`

## Scope
- Replace the dependency tab's three lists with a true interactive dependency graph.
- Use terminal width and height to choose orientation, visible depth, node density, and overflow treatment.
- Make task state, epic membership, epic completion, dependency direction, and the selected exploration focus immediately distinguishable.
- Preserve Ergo View's shared selection, filters, actions, live reload, themes, and cross-platform behavior.

## Research
- Graphviz `dot`: layered directed layout, crossing reduction, shorter edges, and cluster support — https://graphviz.org/docs/layouts/dot/
- Eclipse Layout Kernel: layered layout with ports and hierarchical nodes — https://eclipse.dev/elk/
- Beads Viewer: terminal-native topological layers, orthogonal Unicode routing, adaptive canvas, panning, and focused subgraph depth — https://github.com/Dicklesworthstone/beads_viewer
- Dagster: focused upstream/downstream lineage selection and group filtering — https://docs.dagster.io/concepts/assets/asset-selection-syntax
- Linear: blocked/blocking direction is explicit and dependency lines are actionable — https://linear.app/docs/project-dependencies
- GitHub Actions: node status and dependency edges form the primary graph vocabulary — https://docs.github.com/en/actions/how-tos/monitor-workflows/use-the-visualization-graph

## Decisions
- Use a compact in-process Sugiyama-style layout: topological ranking, deterministic barycentric crossing reduction, then orthogonal routing on a character-cell canvas.
- Keep the default graph focused and adaptive. Spend available cells on the selected node's nearest upstream and downstream context before revealing distant lineage.
- Choose horizontal or vertical flow by measured fit on every resize rather than using a single width breakpoint.
- Render containers as progress-bearing epic cards and leaves as state-bearing task cards. Show parent membership as a tag; only real dependency links receive arrows.
- Keep color semantic but redundant with glyphs, borders, labels, and arrow direction.
- Use spatial keyboard navigation, mouse hit regions, focus history, and direct/adaptive/full-lineage scopes for node exploration.
- Keep layout and graph projection independent of Bubble Tea rendering so geometry is deterministic and thoroughly testable.

## Constraints
- Do not invoke or require Graphviz, ELK, a browser, or a Nerd Font at runtime.
- Preserve the distinction between explicit blocked state and todo work waiting on dependencies.
- Keep all mutation routing through the official `ergo` CLI.
- Avoid hidden clipping: any omitted branch must have an explicit count and discovery path.
- Maintain usable behavior on macOS, Linux, and Windows terminals and under `NO_COLOR`.

## Non-goals
- Scheduling dates or a Gantt chart.
- PageRank, betweenness, critical-path scoring, or automated task prioritization.
- Editing dependencies by drawing edges in this iteration.
- Rendering parent-child containment as if it were a blocking dependency.

# Build the adaptive dependency layout engine

## Goal
- Turn an Ergo snapshot into a deterministic, terminal-sized dependency layout independent of rendering.
- Preserve dependency direction while fitting the most useful neighborhood around the selected node.

## Context
- Ergo graphs are acyclic and may include containers as dependency endpoints.
- Graphviz `dot` and ELK Layered both use hierarchical layers for directed graphs, with crossing and edge-length reduction.
- The default scope should remain useful without asking users to configure graph depth.

## Acceptance Criteria
- A focused graph projection includes the selected node, then expands upstream and downstream breadth-first until the available cell budget is exhausted.
- Hidden branches are represented by stable overflow summaries instead of silently disappearing.
- Nodes are assigned deterministic topological ranks; repeated barycentric sweeps reduce avoidable crossings without changing dependency direction.
- The layout chooses left-to-right or top-to-bottom orientation from available width, height, node dimensions, and visible rank count rather than one fixed breakpoint.
- Ordering is stable across renders and snapshot reloads when the graph has not structurally changed.
- Tasks, containers, dependency edges, and parent membership remain separate concepts in the layout model.
- Diamond, fan-in, fan-out, long-chain, disconnected, multi-container, Unicode-title, tiny-terminal, and large-graph fixtures are covered.
- Layout remains responsive on a synthetic 1,000-node DAG.

## Validation Gates
- `go test -race ./internal/ui -run 'TestGraph|TestAdaptiveGraphLayout'`
- `go test ./internal/ui -run '^$' -bench BenchmarkAdaptiveGraphLayout`
- `go test -race ./...`


## Completion
- Implemented deterministic focused projection, layered ranking, barycentric ordering, adaptive orientation, overflow summaries, and independent geometry.
- Added behavioral fixtures and a 1,000-node benchmark; measured about 6 ms per layout on Apple M1 Pro.

data.text: Implemented and race-tested the adaptive dependency layout engine; 1,000-node benchmark is about 6 ms per layout.

data.title: Simplify and refine the Ergo View visual language
Calm the dependency graph visual language
data.body:
## Goal
- One coherent border and typography system for graph nodes so the graph reads instantly instead of loudly.

## Context
- `internal/ui/graph_render.go` (`drawDependencyNode`, `drawOverflowNode`, `renderGraphHeader`), `internal/ui/styles.go`.
- Today state is triple-encoded (symbol + label + color) and four border families appear at once: rounded, heavy `┏┓`, double `╔╗`, dashed `┄┆`.
- Decisions (made, do not re-open):
  - Node line 1: state symbol + title. Line 2: dim ID, then state label in the state color. Drop the `◇PARENT` chip from graph nodes; the parent stays in the detail pane.
  - Epic nodes: rounded border in the brand color with `◆` prefix — no double-line `╔╗` border.
  - Selected node: heavy border + focus background (as today). Focused-but-not-selected: brand-colored border + `◎` symbol.
  - Overflow cards: title `+N upstream` / `+N downstream`, hint line `d expands depth`.
  - Graph header right side: `depth adaptive · 10 shown · 6 hidden` (plus `focus <ID>` when focus differs from selection). Drop the `left → right` orientation text.

## Acceptance Criteria
- No `╔╗╚╝═║` characters anywhere in the rendered graph.
- Task nodes show only symbol, title, ID, and state label; epic nodes show symbol, title, ID, and progress.
- Overflow cards state their direction and the `d` expand hint.
- `svgRunStyle` / `isBoxDrawing` in `render_snapshot_test.go` still colorize every glyph the graph emits.
- Goldens and `docs/img/*.svg` regenerated and visually reviewed.

## Validation Gates
- `UPDATE_GOLDEN=1 go test ./internal/ui`
- `go test ./...`

data.title: Show container progress as mini bars
data.body:
## Goal
- Containers read at a glance: replace the bare `2/4` fraction with a small progress bar in outline rows, graph epic nodes, and the detail pane.

## Context
- `internal/ui/render.go` (`taskPresentation`, `renderRow`), `internal/ui/graph_render.go` (epic node second line), `internal/ui/detail.go` (Progress section).
- Use a fixed-width 4-cell bar of `▰▱` cells plus the fraction, e.g. `▰▰▱▱ 2/4`. Keep the fraction so exact counts stay visible.
- Depends on the calmed graph node layout from the previous task.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Outline container rows, graph epic nodes, and the container detail Progress section all show the bar + fraction.
- Bar width stays fixed regardless of child count; 0/N and N/N render correctly.
- Narrow widths truncate gracefully (no wrapped rows).

## Validation Gates
- `UPDATE_GOLDEN=1 go test ./internal/ui`
- `go test ./...`

data.title: Make the footer and status line graceful
data.body:
## Goal
- Chrome never renders half-words and stale status messages disappear, so the frame always looks intentional.

## Context
- `internal/ui/render.go` (`renderFooterItems`, `renderStatus`), `internal/ui/model.go`.
- Footer currently joins all hints and truncates mid-item (`? he`). Instead drop whole trailing items until the line fits.
- Transient status messages (`Reloaded external Ergo changes`, `Graph depth: …`) persist forever. Clear `m.status` at the start of every key press before handling it.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Footer at any width ends on a complete `key label` item, never a cut word.
- A status message vanishes on the next key press.
- Unit test covers footer fitting at a width that previously cut mid-word.

## Validation Gates
- `go test ./internal/ui -run 'Footer|Status|Snapshot'`
- `UPDATE_GOLDEN=1 go test ./internal/ui && go test ./...`

data.title: Compact the board columns
data.body:
## Goal
- The board stacks groups by content instead of padding each group to half the column height, removing the large blank blocks.

## Context
- `internal/ui/workflows.go` (`renderBoardColumn`): today `perGroup = max(3, height/2)` and groups pad to multiples of it.
- New layout per column: group header, its tasks (with `+N more` only when the column truly runs out of rows), one blank spacer line, next group. Wide layout keeps the same 3-column group pairing.

## Acceptance Criteria
- No run of more than one blank line between groups in a column.
- `+N more` appears only when the column height is actually exceeded.
- Narrow single-column layout unchanged in structure.

## Validation Gates
- `UPDATE_GOLDEN=1 go test ./internal/ui`
- `go test ./...`

## Scope
- Aesthetic and intuitiveness polish of the existing TUI: dependency graph nodes, container progress, footer/status chrome, board density.

## Decisions
- State is shown once per element: symbol + color carry it; redundant text labels are trimmed where crowded.
- Two border weights only in the graph: rounded (default/epic/overflow) and heavy (selected). Epics differ by brand color + ◆, not by double-line borders.
- Container progress renders as a fixed 4-cell ▰▱ bar plus the exact fraction.

## Non-goals
- No new views, keybindings, layout algorithms, or ergo CLI features.
- No changes to the detail pane markdown rendering.

data.text: Unified borders, decluttered node interiors, clearer overflow cards, leaner header; goldens and docs SVGs regenerated; all tests pass
Progress bars in outline, graph epic nodes, and detail; goldens regenerated; all tests pass
Footer truncates at item boundaries with a unit test across five widths; status clears on next key press
Content-sized group stacking with reserved space for later groups; goldens regenerated; all tests pass

data.title: Make the copy control context-aware and correct
data.body:
## Goal
- Ship the copy shortcut people actually expected: `c` copies what is selected, not always the ID.
- Fix the correctness, presentation, and viewport-fit defects found reviewing PR #12.

## Context
- Branch `codex/copy-task-id`, PR #12 (commit a3a8c65) added `c` and a clickable `copy ID` footer control. It copies `task.ID` unconditionally in every view and focus.
- `task.Body` already holds raw markdown (internal/ergo/model.go:36); the detail pane renders it at internal/ui/detail.go:67. No new plumbing is needed.
- `m.focus` already distinguishes outline from detail (internal/ui/model.go:24). `setView` resets focus to `focusOutline` (internal/ui/model.go:548), so `focusDetail` is an overview-only state.
- `footerItems()` already varies a label by focus (`j/k move` becomes `j/k scroll`). That is the precedent for `copy ID` becoming `copy body`.
- Footer hit-testing derives column ranges from the same layout pass that renders (`footerPlacements`), so render and hit-test must stay in lockstep.

## Decisions
- Payload: overview + `focusDetail` + non-empty body copies raw `task.Body`; everything else copies `task.ID`. Raw markdown, never the glamour output.
- Empty body while detail-focused falls back to `task.ID` and the footer keeps reading `copy ID`. The label always names the actual payload.
- Footer priority: the copy item sits after `a actions`, not at position 2, so `/ search` and `x clear` survive in cramped layouts.
- Modal states: hide the copy item entirely while a dialog, action menu, or search is active. Anything visible must be clickable.
- Help panel: wrap it in a scrolling viewport rather than compacting or filtering rows. The README promises complete in-app help.

## Non-goals
- Sub-selection inside the detail pane (copying one dependency or result line). The pane is a single rendered blob in a viewport; making its sections selectable is a much larger change.
- Copying the full detail as reconstructed markdown. `renderTaskDetail` emits styled terminal output, not markdown.

## Validation Gates
- `go test -race ./...`
- `go vet ./...`
- `gofmt -l internal/` prints nothing
- Goldens and doc SVGs regenerate with `UPDATE_GOLDEN=1 go test ./internal/ui`

data.title: Make the footer row claim its own mouse clicks
data.body:
## Goal
- A click on the footer row must never leak into view handling. Today a footer click that misses the copy control silently changes pane focus or moves the selection.

## Context
- `updateMouseClick` (internal/ui/model.go:329) calls `updateFooterMouseClick`, which returns nil unless the click lands on the copy control. Execution then falls through into the overview and graph click handling below it.
- Verified, not theoretical: on a 120x28 overview, a left click at X=110, Y=height-1 (over `x clear` / `q quit`) flips `m.focus` from `focusOutline` (0) to `focusDetail` (1).
- The row-selection path computes `rowIndex = message.Y - 3`, so at `Y = m.height-1` it resolves to `height-4`. With more rows than the 6-row test fixture that lands inside `m.rows` and selects a row the user never clicked.
- This misbehavior predates PR #12, but that PR turned the footer into a real click target, so the footer must now own its row.
- Separately, `m.status` is cleared only in the `tea.KeyPressMsg` branch (internal/ui/model.go:180). A mouse-driven copy leaves "Copied X to clipboard" in the header indefinitely, across reload ticks and later clicks.

## Acceptance Criteria
- `updateMouseClick` delegates the whole footer row to the footer handler and returns without running overview or graph handling, e.g. `if message.Y == m.height-1 { return m.updateFooterMouseClick(message) }`.
- A left click on the footer row that misses the copy control changes neither `m.focus` nor `m.selected`, in narrow overview, wide overview, board, and dependencies.
- Hit-test bounds stay half-open: a click at `placement.start` copies, a click at `placement.end` does not. Cover both edges with a test.
- Mouse clicks clear `m.status` the way key presses do, so a stale "Copied ..." message cannot persist.
- Clicks above the footer row behave exactly as before; existing mouse tests still pass unchanged.

## Validation Gates
- `go test -race ./internal/ui`
- `go vet ./...`
- `gofmt -l internal/` prints nothing

data.title: Correct the copy control footer placement and visibility
data.body:
## Goal
- Stop the copy control from evicting more useful footer hints, and stop drawing it in states where it cannot fire.

## Context
- `footerItems()` (internal/ui/render.go:337) inserts `m.copyIDFooterItem()` at index 1 in all three branches. The PR #12 golden diffs show exactly what that evicts:
  - `/ search` in narrow overview (72 cols) and standard dependencies
  - `x clear` in wide overview and board
  - `a actions` in narrow dependencies
- Every branch already contains an `a actions` item, so "immediately after `a actions`" is a uniform rule across all three.
- `viewContent` (internal/ui/render.go:65) renders the footer unconditionally, so the control is drawn over dialogs, the action menu, and search. `updateFooterMouseClick` then swallows those clicks, leaving a visible control that does nothing.
- `copyIDFooterItem` already returns a zero `footerItem{}` when nothing is selected, and `compactFooterItems` filters it out. Reuse that mechanism for the modal states rather than adding a second one.

## Acceptance Criteria
- The copy item is ordered immediately after `a actions` in all three `footerItems()` branches.
- After the reorder, `/ search` is visible again in narrow overview at 72 cols and in standard dependencies, and `x clear` is visible again in wide overview and board. Assert this, do not just eyeball the goldens.
- `copyIDFooterItem` returns an empty item when `m.dialog != nil`, `m.actionMenu`, or `m.searching`, so the control disappears from the footer in those states.
- Because hit-testing derives from the same `footerItems()`, the now-redundant modal guards inside `updateFooterMouseClick` are removed rather than left duplicated.
- Clicking where the control used to sit during a dialog, action menu, or search copies nothing and sets no status. Cover the dialog case, which PR #12 left untested.
- Goldens and doc SVGs regenerated; `git diff docs/img/` contains only the intended footer text changes.

## Validation Gates
- `UPDATE_GOLDEN=1 go test ./internal/ui`, then `go test -race ./...`
- `go vet ./...`
- `gofmt -l internal/` prints nothing

data.title: Copy the task body when the detail pane is focused
data.body:
## Goal
- Make `c` copy what is actually selected: the body markdown while reading a task detail, the ID everywhere else. This is the feature PR #12 was meant to deliver.

## Context
- `copySelectedID` (internal/ui/model.go:363) copies `task.ID` unconditionally, consulting neither view nor focus.
- `task.Body` is raw markdown on the struct (internal/ergo/model.go:36). Copy it raw. The pane's glamour output (internal/ui/detail.go:70) is ANSI-escaped and hard-wrapped to pane width, useless on a clipboard.
- `m.focus == focusDetail` is the only signal available for "the body is what is selected" — the detail pane is one viewport blob with no sub-selection. `setView` resets focus (internal/ui/model.go:548), so `focusDetail` occurs only in overview, including the narrow layout where the detail replaces the outline.
- `footerItems()` already swaps `j/k move` for `j/k scroll` when `m.focus == focusDetail`. Follow that precedent for the copy label instead of inventing a new mechanism.
- Guard body presence with `strings.TrimSpace(task.Body) != ""`, matching the detail pane at internal/ui/detail.go:67.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Overview + `focusDetail` + non-empty body copies raw `task.Body`. Every other combination copies `task.ID`.
- Empty body while detail-focused falls back to `task.ID`.
- The footer label reads `copy body` exactly when the body will be copied and `copy ID` otherwise, including the empty-body fallback. The label must never disagree with the payload.
- The status message names the payload, e.g. "Copied TOKENS body to clipboard" against "Copied TOKENS to clipboard".
- Board and dependencies always copy the ID, regardless of any stale focus state.
- Keyboard `c` and the footer click resolve to the identical payload; test both paths for the body case.
- Containers follow the same rule as tasks (they carry bodies too).
- Docs updated: the in-app help row (internal/ui/render.go:399), README.md:45, and the key table at README.md:79 all describe the context-aware behavior.
- Goldens and doc SVGs regenerated for the detail-focused overview cases.

## Validation Gates
- `UPDATE_GOLDEN=1 go test ./internal/ui`, then `go test -race ./...`
- `go vet ./...`
- `gofmt -l internal/` prints nothing
- Manual: `go run ./cmd/ev`, tab into the detail pane on a task with a body, press `c`, paste elsewhere and confirm raw markdown arrives

data.title: Keep the help panel inside the viewport
data.body:
## Goal
- The help overlay renders more lines than the terminal has, clipping or displacing the footer.

## Context
- Reported by Codex on PR #12 against internal/ui/render.go:399 and confirmed by measurement, not just arithmetic:
  - overview renders 26 lines at terminal heights 24 and 25; it first fits at 26
  - dependencies renders 31 lines at heights 29 and 30; it first fits at 31
- `renderHelp` (internal/ui/render.go:387) builds 19 rows for overview and 24 for dependencies, wraps them in `helpPanel` (DoubleBorder plus `Padding(1,2)`, so 4 rows of frame), then calls `lipgloss.Place` with `m.contentHeight()` (`m.height-3`). `lipgloss.Place` does not crop oversized content, so the excess silently pushes the footer off screen.
- The `c` row added by PR #12 is what regressed h25 and h30 exactly; overflow already existed at h24 and h29 before the PR. Fix both, not just the regression.
- The detail pane already uses a bubbles viewport. Reuse that pattern rather than introducing a new scrolling mechanism.
- While `m.help` is true, `updateKey` (internal/ui/model.go:222) consumes every key except `?`, `esc`, `q`, and `enter`, so scroll keys must be wired in explicitly.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Help content scrolls inside a viewport sized to `m.contentHeight()`; the rendered view is never taller than `m.height` at any size.
- `j`/`k`, arrow keys, page keys, and the mouse wheel scroll the help panel while it is open.
- `?`, `esc`, `q`, and `enter` still close it.
- Scroll position resets to the top each time help opens.
- The panel signals that more content exists when it overflows, so a truncated list is not mistaken for the whole list.
- The existing `m.help` early return in `updateMouseClick` still stops help-mode clicks from reaching the views.
- Explicitly verified at the regression sizes: overview at 24 and 25, dependencies at 29 and 30.

## Validation Gates
- `go test -race ./internal/ui`
- `go vet ./...`
- `gofmt -l internal/` prints nothing
- Manual: `go run ./cmd/ev` in an 80x24 terminal, press `?`, scroll to the last line, confirm the footer is intact throughout

data.title: Add a viewport-fit regression guard
data.body:
## Goal
- Catch the whole class of "rendered view exceeds the terminal" defects automatically, instead of one bug report at a time.

## Context
- The help overflow shipped because no test renders the help overlay at a tight height. `assertFits` already exists in internal/ui/model_test.go but is applied to only a few cases.
- Overflow is silent by construction: `lipgloss.Place` does not crop, so extra lines push the footer off screen without failing anything. Only an explicit dimension assertion catches it.
- Overlays other than help (action menu, each dialog kind) have never been dimension-checked either and may already overflow.

## Acceptance Criteria
- A table-driven test asserts that `model.View().Content` has at most `height` lines and no line wider than `width`, across the full matrix:
  - views: overview, board, dependencies
  - overlays: none, help open, action menu open, and each dialog kind
  - focus: outline and detail
  - sizes: 40x12, 72x20, 80x24, 100x25, 120x29, 120x30, and one oversized case
- Measure display width with `ansi.StringWidth` on styled output, consistent with the existing helpers.
- Failure output names the exact combination and reports actual against allowed dimensions, so a regression is diagnosable without a debugger.
- Demonstrated to catch the real bug: temporarily restore the unbounded `renderHelp` and confirm the guard fails, then restore the fix. Record the observed failure in the completion message.
- Any additional overflow the matrix uncovers is either fixed here if small, or filed as a new task with its exact reproduction.

## Validation Gates
- `go test -race ./internal/ui`
- `go vet ./...`
- `gofmt -l internal/` prints nothing

data.title: Tidy the footer layout internals
data.body:
## Goal
- Remove the drift and aliasing hazards left by the footer refactor, with no behavior change.

## Context
- Runs last, once the behavioral footer tasks have landed, so it refactors settled code instead of racing it.
- Everything below is in internal/ui/render.go unless noted.

## Acceptance Criteria
- `const separator = "  ·  "` is declared once at package scope instead of separately inside `footerPlacements` and `renderFooterItems`. These two must agree exactly or hit-test columns drift silently with no test failure, which is the sharpest edge in the current code.
- The x-origin in `footerPlacements` (`m.styles.footer.GetPaddingLeft()`) is either documented as depending on `styles.app` carrying no padding (internal/ui/styles.go:76) and the footer being the last of exactly `m.height` lines, or derived so it cannot break silently if `app` later gains a frame.
- `updateFooterMouseClick` moves out of render.go, matching the project convention that mouse handlers live in model.go and graph_interaction.go (`updateGraphMouseClick`).
- `compactFooterItems` filters in place via `items[:0]`, mutating the caller backing array. Either document that contract or make it non-aliasing.
- The footer stops deep-cloning a task every frame: `copyIDFooterItem` currently reaches `selectedTask()` then `Snapshot.Task()` then `cloneTask` (internal/ergo/model.go:89) purely to test whether a selection exists. Use a non-cloning check.
- `footerActionNone` is either used or removed.
- Strictly no behavior change: no golden or SVG file is modified.

## Validation Gates
- `go test -race ./...` with no golden regeneration
- `git diff --stat internal/ui/testdata docs/img` is empty
- `go vet ./...`
- `gofmt -l internal/` prints nothing
- `go test -bench=. -run=^$ ./internal/ui` shows no regression against the pre-change baseline

data.text: Fixed footer-row click ownership and stale mouse status; added regressions for all views and half-open hit bounds; verified with race tests, vet, and gofmt.
Reordered footer priorities, hid inactive copy controls during modal input, and regenerated footer-only goldens/docs; verified with race tests, vet, and gofmt.

Made copy payload context-aware from one resolver; covered raw task/container body copy, ID fallback, stale focus, keyboard/mouse parity, docs, goldens, and live OSC52 output; verified with race tests, vet, and gofmt.

## Goal

## Context
- Supersedes the body-only rule shipped in KARLAW (commit 67af1e6). That is a deliberate replacement, not a regression.
- The seam already exists: `selectedCopyTarget()` (internal/ui/model.go:398) returns `copyTarget{text, label, status}`, and both the footer label and the clipboard payload derive from it. Only its detail-focus branch plus a new markdown emitter are needed; `copySelection`, hit-testing, and footer wiring stay as they are.
- `renderTaskDetail` (internal/ui/detail.go:24) is the source of truth for what the pane shows, but it emits styled terminal output: lipgloss styles plus glamour-rendered markdown hard-wrapped to pane width. It cannot be reused for the clipboard. Write a parallel markdown emitter over the same `ergo.Task`.
- Pane section order to mirror (internal/ui/detail.go:27-95): state label and ID; title; `claimed by` when set; `container` when `ParentID` is set; `Depends on`; `Unlocks`; `Progress` for containers; `Description` (the body); `Activity`; `Results`.
- `taskLabel` (internal/ui/detail.go:116) returns a styled string; a plain-text variant is needed for container and dependency lines.
- The empty-body fallback from KARLAW becomes obsolete. The detail always renders state, ID, and title, so there is always something to copy: detail focus plus a selection always copies the detail markdown.
- Note for the in-flight 4UAEX6: once the label depends only on view, focus, and whether anything is selected — not on body content — its non-cloning footer check stays achievable. Do not reintroduce a per-frame body read.

## Decisions
- Mirror the pane exactly, including Activity and Results. The rule is "what you see is what you copy"; a partial subset reintroduces the guessing this task exists to remove.
- Emit clean markdown: no ANSI, no glamour, no lipgloss, no wrapping to pane width. The body is embedded raw.
- The footer label becomes `copy detail`. `copy ID` remains for outline focus, board, and dependencies.
- Body-only copy is superseded, not preserved. If both are wanted later that is a second binding and a separate task.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Overview + `focusDetail` + a selection copies markdown mirroring the pane; every other context still copies `task.ID`.
- Output contains no ANSI escapes — assert `ansi.Strip(out) == out` — and no wrapping introduced by the exporter.
- Sections appear in pane order and are omitted exactly when the pane omits them: no `claimed by` when unclaimed, no `Depends on` when there are none, `Progress` only for containers, no `Description` when the body is blank.
- Container progress is carried as text (`3 of 7 children complete`), not the mini bar glyphs.
- Container, dependency, and unlock references carry both ID and title in plain text.
- The raw body is embedded verbatim under a `Description` heading; markdown inside it is neither re-rendered nor escaped.
- A drift test asserts that every section the pane renders for a fully populated fixture also appears in the exported markdown, so the two renderers cannot silently diverge.
- Status message reflects the payload, e.g. `Copied TOKENS detail to clipboard`.
- Footer reads `copy detail` under detail focus and `copy ID` elsewhere; the label never disagrees with the payload.
- Keyboard `c` and the footer click produce byte-identical output.
- Docs updated: the in-app help row in internal/ui/render.go, README.md:45, and the key table row at README.md:79.
- Goldens and doc SVGs regenerated for the detail-focused overview cases.

- `go vet ./...`
- `gofmt -l internal/` prints nothing
- Manual: `go run ./cmd/ev`, focus the detail pane on a container that has dependencies, activity, and results; press `c`; paste into a markdown viewer and confirm it reads as the pane does

## Goal
- Ship the copy shortcut people actually expected: `c` copies what is selected, not always the ID.
- Fix the correctness, presentation, and viewport-fit defects found reviewing PR #12.

## Context
- Branch `codex/copy-task-id`, PR #12 (commit a3a8c65) added `c` and a clickable `copy ID` footer control. It copies `task.ID` unconditionally in every view and focus.

data.title: Copy ID and title from the outline
data.body:
## Goal
- Outline selection copied the bare ID, which pastes as an opaque token. Copy `ID  Title` so the reference reads on its own.

## Outcome
- `selectedCopyTarget()` outline branch returns `taskReference(task)` = `ID` + two spaces + `Title`, falling back to the bare ID when the title is empty.
- Footer label changed from `copy ID` to `copy ref`, because `copy ID` no longer names the payload.
- Status message carries the full precision: `Copied SNOWNB ID and title to clipboard`.
- Detail-focus behavior is unchanged and still exports the whole pane as Markdown, body included.

## Label sizing note
- `copy ID+title` was rejected: the narrow (72 col) overview footer had only 5 columns of slack, and the 6 extra columns dropped the copy control off the footer entirely, undoing PNYOCY. `copy ref` costs 1 column and keeps `/ search` visible.

## Verification
- `go test -race ./...`, `go vet ./...`, `gofmt -l internal/` all clean.
- Goldens and doc SVGs regenerated; narrow overview footer confirmed as `j/k move · 1/2/3 views · / search · a actions · c copy ref`.
- Checked against the live repo graph: outline gives `SNOWNB  Copy the whole detail view as markdown`; detail gives 4960 bytes including `## Description`.

## Note on the reported missing body
- Could not reproduce. The body is present in the detail export via three independent checks: package fixture, live `.ergo` snapshot, and a scan showing all 24 tasks carry bodies.
- Most likely cause of the observed behavior: `/opt/homebrew/bin/ev` on PATH was built 23 Jul 21:50, predating every commit in this epic.

data.title: Make clipboard writes reach the clipboard the user is looking at
data.body:
## Goal
- Make a reported copy actually land on the clipboard the user is looking at, and make the status line tell the truth when it cannot.
- Close the review findings on PR #13 (`codex/native-clipboard`, base `main`, commits 1605d59 and 858326c).

## Context
- PR #13 replaced the OSC52-only copy with a native system clipboard write (`github.com/atotto/clipboard`), keeping OSC52 as a fallback, behind a `clipboardQueue` in internal/ui/clipboard.go.
- The sequencing design is sound and must be preserved: `request()` checks `isLatest` *inside* `writeMu` (internal/ui/clipboard.go:36), so a stale request that acquires the lock after a newer one bumped the counter skips its write. `Update` re-checks `isLatest` (internal/ui/model.go:198) to drop stale status. Do not "simplify" either check away.
- No new supply-chain surface: `charm.land/bubbles/v2` already required `atotto/clipboard@v0.1.4`. The PR only promotes it from indirect to direct.
- No injection risk: the darwin path is `exec.Command("pbcopy")` with content on stdin, no shell.
- Verified absent in the current code: any `SSH_*` check, any timeout, any context on the write.

## Decisions
- Remote sessions: when `SSH_CONNECTION` or `SSH_TTY` is set, skip the native write and use OSC52, which is the only channel that reaches the local machine. Local sessions keep the verified native path unchanged.
- Large payloads: when the OSC52 path carries more than a conservative threshold, say so in the status line. Do not silently send something likely to arrive truncated, and do not refuse the copy outright.
- Keep OSC52 as the fallback rather than verifying by read-back. A read-back over SSH reads the *remote* clipboard, which would match, so it cannot detect the very failure this epic exists to fix.

## Non-goals
- Replacing `atotto/clipboard` with a cgo-based library. It is already in the tree, pinned with bubbles, and shells out safely.
- Chunked or multiplexed OSC52 for oversized payloads. Warning is enough until someone reports real truncation.

## Validation Gates
- `go test -race ./...`
- `go vet ./...`
- `gofmt -l internal/` prints nothing
- No test may write to the real system clipboard

data.title: Prefer the terminal clipboard in remote sessions
data.body:
## Goal
- Over SSH, a copy currently reports success while the users clipboard never changes. Route remote sessions to the only channel that can reach them.

## Context
- On macOS over SSH, `pbcopy` runs on the *remote* Mac and succeeds. Success means `message.err == nil`, so the OSC52 fallback at internal/ui/model.go:201 never fires, and the status reads `Copied TOKENS ID and title to clipboard` while the local pasteboard is untouched.
- This is the same defect PR #13 set out to fix, relocated. Its own Root cause section says Ergo View "immediately reported a successful copy without verifying that the system pasteboard changed" — that is exactly what still happens remotely.
- Linux mostly self-corrects: `atotto/clipboard` errors when no utility is found, and `xclip` fails without `DISPLAY`, so the fallback fires. This is primarily a macOS-over-SSH defect, but the fix should not be macOS-specific.
- Verified absent: no `SSH_CONNECTION`, `SSH_TTY`, or any other remote-session check exists anywhere in internal/ui.
- Read-back verification is not an option and must not be proposed as one: over SSH it reads the remote clipboard, which matches what was just written, so it cannot detect this failure.

## Acceptance Criteria
- A remote-session predicate returns true when `SSH_CONNECTION` or `SSH_TTY` is non-empty, and is injectable or otherwise overridable so tests never mutate real process environment.
- In a remote session `copySelection` returns the OSC52 command directly and performs no native write.
- In a local session behavior is byte-for-byte unchanged: native write first, OSC52 only on error, sequencing intact.
- The status message distinguishes the two paths, so a remote user is not told a native copy happened. Wording is settled in the sibling status task; here just do not claim the native path.
- Tests cover: remote session issues no native write; local session still does; and the remote path still produces the correct payload for both an outline reference and a detail export.
- The `isLatest`-inside-the-mutex check and the `Update` re-check both survive unchanged.

## Validation Gates
- `go test -race ./internal/ui`
- `go vet ./...`
- `gofmt -l internal/` prints nothing
- Manual, if a second machine is available: `ssh` into this Mac, run `ev`, press `c`, confirm the payload arrives on the *local* clipboard

data.title: Bound the native clipboard write
data.body:
## Goal
- A hanging clipboard utility currently wedges every future copy for the life of the process. Bound the write.

## Context
- `clipboardQueue.request` holds `writeMu` across the entire `q.writer(target.text)` call (internal/ui/clipboard.go:34-43), which shells out to an external process.
- If that process hangs, `writeMu` is never released. Every later copy blocks on it forever and each queued Bubble Tea command goroutine leaks. There is no recovery short of restarting Ergo View.
- `xclip` is the classic offender: it forks and holds the X selection rather than exiting. Low probability on macOS, but the consequence is unbounded.
- `atotto/clipboard` exposes no context-aware API, so the write must be run on its own goroutine and waited on with a timeout.
- Verified absent: no timeout, no context, no deadline anywhere in the clipboard path.

## Acceptance Criteria
- The native write is bounded by a timeout. Pick a value that is generous for a healthy `pbcopy` and short enough not to feel stuck; record the number and the reasoning in the completion message.
- A timed-out write is reported as a failure, so the existing OSC52 fallback fires and the user still gets their payload.
- `writeMu` is released when the wait times out. A hung writer must not block the next copy, and the sequencing guarantees must still hold for every request that follows.
- The orphaned goroutine from a hung write is left in a state that cannot corrupt later writes: it must not be able to write its stale payload after a newer request has completed.
- A test with a writer that blocks until released proves the next copy still succeeds while the first is stuck.
- A test proves a timed-out write produces the OSC52 fallback.
- No test sleeps for the real timeout duration; the timeout must be injectable.

## Validation Gates
- `go test -race ./internal/ui`
- `go test -race ./internal/ui -run TestClipboard -count=50` to shake out flakiness in the new concurrency
- `go vet ./...`
- `gofmt -l internal/` prints nothing

data.title: Make copy status tell the truth
data.body:
## Goal
- The status line should describe the copy that actually happened, on the channel it actually used, and admit when the payload may not survive.

## Context
- Two separate honesty gaps, both in the async completion path added by PR #13.

### Large OSC52 payloads may truncate silently
- PR #12 made copy payloads multi-kilobyte. A real detail export measured 4960 bytes, roughly 6.6 KB once base64-encoded.
- Many terminals and tmux cap OSC52 well below that. The fallback can therefore deliver a truncated payload under a status claiming the terminal clipboard was used.
- This predates PR #13, but that PR makes the fallback load-bearing, so it now matters.

### A late completion can describe a context the user already left
- Status is set when `clipboardWriteMsg` arrives (internal/ui/model.go:205), not when the key is pressed.
- Press `c` then `j` quickly: the `j` handler clears status (internal/ui/model.go:208), then the async completion re-sets `Copied TOKENS ...` after the selection has already moved.
- The statement is true but arrives detached from what the user is now looking at. Sub-millisecond on macOS; visible behind a slow utility or the new timeout.

## Acceptance Criteria
- When the OSC52 path carries a payload above a conservative threshold, the status says so plainly, naming the size, e.g. `System clipboard unavailable; sent 4.9 KB via terminal — large payloads may truncate`.
- The threshold is a named constant with a comment explaining where the number came from. Do not pretend to know each terminals real limit.
- Normal-size fallbacks keep the existing shorter message; the warning is not attached to every fallback.
- A completion that arrives after the user has acted again does not overwrite the status. Track this so a late message is dropped rather than displayed out of context.
- A superseded copy still produces no status at all, as today. Do not regress the `isLatest` behavior while adding this.
- Tests cover: a large fallback warns and names a size; a small fallback does not; a completion arriving after an intervening key press is dropped; a completion arriving with no intervening action still reports.

## Validation Gates
- `go test -race ./internal/ui`
- `go vet ./...`
- `gofmt -l internal/` prints nothing

data.title: Make the clipboard writer injectable
data.body:
## Goal
- Make "unit tests never touch the real clipboard" a structural guarantee instead of a convention one new test can break.

## Context
- `New()` wires the live `writeSystemClipboard` unconditionally (internal/ui/model.go:113). Only the `testModel` helper swaps it out (internal/ui/model_test.go).
- Thirteen other tests build models through `New(...)` carrying the live writer: actions_test.go, graph_interaction_test.go, graph_render_test.go, render_snapshot_test.go, render_bench_test.go, and several in model_test.go.
- None of them trigger a copy today, so PR #13s claim is accurate right now. It holds by luck of coverage, not by construction: the next test that presses `c` on a `New()`-built model writes to the developers real pasteboard during `go test`.
- Related latent defect: graph_render.go:330 constructs `Model{snapshot: snapshot}` directly, leaving `clipboard` nil. Safe today because it only calls `taskPresentation`, but `copySelection` on that value is a nil dereference.

## Acceptance Criteria
- The clipboard writer is supplied through `Options`, defaulting to `writeSystemClipboard` when the caller leaves it unset, so production wiring is unchanged.
- `testModel` sets it through that seam rather than reaching into the struct field afterwards.
- Every test that constructs a model via `New(...)` either routes through `testModel` or passes an explicit test writer. No test path can reach `writeSystemClipboard`.
- A guard makes the guarantee enforceable rather than aspirational: either the copy path fails loudly on a nil queue, or a test asserts that no model built by the test helpers carries the system writer. State which approach was taken and why.
- The nil-queue path in graph_render.go:330 is made safe, by construction or by an explicit guard in `copySelection`.
- Purely structural. No user-visible behavior changes and no golden or SVG file is modified.

## Validation Gates
- `go test -race ./...`
- `git diff --stat internal/ui/testdata docs/img` is empty
- `go vet ./...`
- `gofmt -l internal/` prints nothing

data.text: Added an unexported Options seam with the production writer as the default, routed every test constructor through a no-op writer, and guarded partial Models with no clipboard queue. Verified with go test -race ./internal/ui; no golden or SVG changes.

Detected SSH_CONNECTION or SSH_TTY through an injectable predicate, routed remote copies directly to OSC52 without a native write, and superseded older queued writes before sending. Covered outline, detail, local detection, and stale native requests; go test -race ./internal/ui and go vet ./... pass.

Bound native-copy completions to the initiating user interaction, so a later key or mouse action drops stale status while the latest-copy sequence check remains intact. Added a 3 KiB raw-text OSC52 warning threshold, keeping the encoded sequence near a conservative 4 KiB compatibility budget, with size-aware status for large fallbacks and remote copies. Race tests, 50 repeated copy tests, and vet pass.

Not safe or worthwhile as specified. atotto/clipboard exposes an opaque, non-cancelable write. Timing it out in a goroutine can release writeMu and let a newer copy complete, but the orphaned older call may still return later and overwrite the clipboard with stale content, violating both this task's acceptance criteria and the latest-request-wins invariant. A correct solution requires a cancelable platform adapter and broader cross-platform replacement; defer until an actual hang is reported or the dependency exposes cancellation.

data.body:
## Goal
- Prevent a hanging native clipboard utility from wedging every later copy for the life of the process.

## Context
- `atotto/clipboard` exposes an opaque, non-cancelable write.
- A timed-out write may still finish later and overwrite a newer OSC52 copy. This residual risk is accepted because permanent copy failure is worse.
- The queue must limit that risk to one orphaned native write and preserve copy availability.

## Decision
- Give the first native write a two-second deadline.
- On timeout, permanently degrade the queue for the rest of the process.
- A degraded queue starts no more native writes and routes every later copy through the existing OSC52 fallback.
- Document the accepted stale-write risk beside the concurrency logic so Ergo pruning cannot erase it.

## Acceptance Criteria
- A native write that exceeds two seconds returns a failure and triggers OSC52.
- `writeMu` is released after the deadline, allowing later requests to complete.
- After the first timeout, no further native writer call starts.
- At most one orphaned native write can exist.
- The timeout mechanism is injectable; tests do not sleep for the production duration.
- A deterministic race test proves a second copy falls back while the first writer remains blocked.
- Remove `supersede()` and its production-impossible test because remote-session mode is fixed when `New` constructs the model.

## Validation Gates
- `go test -race ./...`
- `go test -race ./internal/ui -run 'TestClipboard|TestLatestCopyRequestWins' -count=50`
- `go vet ./...`
- `gofmt -l internal/` prints nothing

data.text: Revised after review: added a two-second circuit breaker around native writes. On timeout the queue permanently degrades, starts no further native writes, and routes later copies through OSC52; this bounds the hang to one orphaned writer. The code documents the accepted possibility that the non-cancelable orphan may later land stale content. Removed supersede() and its production-impossible test. Verified with the full race suite, 50 repeated clipboard race runs, vet, formatting, and Windows cross-build.

data.title: Resolve clipboard delivery design debt from issue #14
Centralize clipboard delivery ownership
data.body:
## Goal
- Make one clipboard destination own native-versus-terminal routing, fallback, circuit breaking, and latest-request sequencing.

## Context
- Issue #14 identifies split orchestration between `Model` and `clipboardQueue`.
- PR #13 already removed `supersede()` and added a two-second circuit breaker; preserve those behaviors.
- `Model` should retain UI-interaction freshness because the clipboard module cannot know whether unrelated UI input makes a completion out of context.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Replace `clipboardQueue` with a destination whose `copy(text)` operation chooses the delivery channel and returns a delivery outcome plus any OSC52 command.
- The destination checks its own latest-request token before and after native delivery; stale messages require no model-side sequence check.
- Replace `Options.clipboardWriter` and `Options.remoteSession` with one unexported clipboard destination.
- Keep a single pending interaction token in `Model`; do not pass it through the destination.
- Preserve native success, SSH terminal delivery, native-error fallback, timeout degradation, and latest-request-wins behavior.

## Validation Gates
- `go test -race ./internal/ui`
- `go test -race ./internal/ui -run 'TestClipboard|TestLatestCopyRequestWins|TestRemote' -count=50`
- `go vet ./...`
- `gofmt -l internal/` prints nothing

data.title: Derive every copy status from its outcome
data.body:
## Goal
- Make every copy status identify what was copied without storing channel-specific pre-rendered strings in the target.

## Context
- Status is a function of copy subject, delivery channel, and payload size.
- The target should define one subject phrase per payload kind; the delivery outcome should define channel, size, and error.

## Acceptance Criteria
- `copyTarget` contains text, footer label, and one subject phrase; it contains no pre-rendered status.
- One formatter covers native, direct terminal, small fallback, large direct terminal, and large fallback outcomes.
- Every rendered status names the task ID and payload kind.
- Large terminal statuses retain the size and truncation warning.
- Table-driven tests cover the complete outcome matrix and prevent missing subjects.
- Existing UI behavior and golden/SVG artifacts remain unchanged.

## Validation Gates
- `go test -race ./...`
- `go test -race ./internal/ui -run 'TestCopy|TestClipboard|TestLatestCopyRequestWins|TestRemote' -count=50`
- `go vet ./...`
- `gofmt -l internal/` prints nothing
- Windows AMD64 cross-build through `go test -exec=/usr/bin/true ./...`
- `git diff --stat internal/ui/testdata docs/img` is empty

data.text: Replaced clipboardQueue with a destination that owns remote routing, native delivery, OSC52 fallback commands, timeout degradation, and pre/post-write latest-request checks. Model now retains pending copy context and interaction freshness locally; Options exposes one unexported destination seam. Verified race tests, 50 repeated clipboard/latest/remote runs, vet, and formatting.

Replaced pre-rendered native/terminal target strings with one subject phrase and a single formatter over subject, channel, and size. All five delivery outcomes now name the task and payload kind; large terminal paths retain size and truncation warnings. Added a complete table-driven matrix and subject regression. Full race suite, 50 repeated copy tests, vet, formatting, Windows cross-build, and golden/SVG diff checks pass.

Final preservation check: late UI interactions suppress only clipboard status; they do not suppress an already-selected OSC52 delivery command. Added a 50-run race regression for SSH copy followed immediately by navigation.
